EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: James D'Amour, resident, spoke in opposition to CA-9, regarding The Enclave of Ann Arbor Development Agreement. He urged Council to pull this item from the Consent Agenda.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: James D'Amour - 2857 Packard - The Enclave of Ann Arbor Development Agreement (CA-9) (phone)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Karen Wight, resident, spoke in opposition to item CA-9, urging Council to pull the item from the Consent Agenda and allow for more discussion.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Karen Wight - 2857 Packard - The Enclave of Ann Arbor Development Agreement (CA-9) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Anne Bannister, resident and former Councilmember, spoke in opposition to item CA-9, regarding The Enclave of Ann Arbor Development Agreement.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Anne Bannister - 2857 Packard - The Enclave of Ann Arbor Development Agreement (CA-9) (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Chuck Kieffer, resident, expressed his concerns regarding ICE in Ann Arbor. He urged Council to ban ICE agents from City buildings and to make these facilities safe spaces for City residents.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Chuck Kieffer - Collaboration with ICE (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Alex Lowe, resident, spoke about his safety concerns in Ann Arbor. He expressed concern regarding Vision Zero, traffic congestion, and about his identity as an immigrant.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Alex Lowe - What we can and cannot do to improve safety (Zoom)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Jeremy Haley, Ypsilanti Township resident, spoke about the amount of interest the City would have to pay on a 30-year bond.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Jeremy Haley - General comment (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Catherine James, Taylor City resident, spoke about her ongoing lawsuit against the Washtenaw County Sheriff's Office.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Catherine James - Suppressed evidence (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Henry Herskovitz, resident, spoke about Holocaust history and education. He questioned some of the previous beliefs surrounding the events.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Henry Herskovitz - Holocaust education in the Ann Arbor Public Schools (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Kathy Griswold, resident, spoke about concerns she has regarding the City's work on transportation safety.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Kathy Griswold - Opportunities in 2026 (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Blaine Coleman, resident, expressed concern about national politics and the rise in racist rhetoric at the national level.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Blaine Coleman - We are against military aid to Israel (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Pwon Bailey spoke about politics in Ann Arbor.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Pwon Bailey - View of Ann Arbor from a lens that isn't political (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Chuck Ream, resident and Ward Three Council candidate, spoke in opposition to the proposed Comprehensive Land Use Plan. He urged other residents to run for public office.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Chuck Ream - Comprehensive Land Use Plan (in person)

EventItems.EventItemMinutesNote: Laura Sanders, Dexter Township resident, spoke about racial profiling and the presence of ICE in Washtenaw County. She provided examples of disappearances of local residents by ICE agents.
EventItems.EventItemTitle: Laura Sanders - Immigration (in person)
